title: Delulu or solulu: they held the door
old_caption: They held the door and Cancer was ready to bring out the family photo album. Then Cancer asked about coffee and got a real yes. Manners are a start, not a proposal.

title: Delulu or solulu: a follow-up question
old_caption: Aquarius read two follow-up questions as destiny, asked about a date, and got "as friends? I'd love that!" Still a win: now Aquarius knows, and it made a friend.

title: Cancer Frames a Text
old_caption:
Cancer got a same-day reply and had it framed. Then someone remembered the talk with their mom, and the frame quietly hit the floor.
What tiny thing did you once treat like a proposal?

title: Leo Gets a Thumbs-Up
old_caption: One like on a photo and Leo is already thanking the academy. The person who saved a front-row seat at the recital, though? That's the real standing ovation.

title: Libra Gets Asked
old_caption: Being asked where to eat should not require a parade. Libra threw one anyway. Then Gemini booked the place Libra mentioned once, in July. Tag your listener.

title: Virgo Grades a Text
old_caption: A period at the end of a text earned a gold star. Seven o'clock-ish earned an A+. A whole plan made for them? Virgo dropped the clipboard. Which grade would your last date get?

title: Aquarius Gets a Good Morning
old_caption: Aquarius commissioned a statue for a good-morning text. Fair. Then Sagittarius asked to hear the whole theory, all night, and the bar went straight to the ceiling.

title: Taurus and the Last Dumpling
old_caption: Not sharing fries with someone who said they weren't hungry: valid. The slow stare over the last dumpling: a little petty. Missing your cozy night: valid, so say it out loud.

title: Gemini Renames a Contact
old_caption: Saving them in your phone as Mr. Late is petty, and Gemini knows it. Wanting someone to ask about your day is not. Which one have you done this week?

title: Scorpio's Dramatic Exit
old_caption: Scorpio remembers what you wore on date one, swept out of the room in a cape (to the kitchen), and still wants to know where this is going. Two out of three, honestly.
